To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CO2/H+-mediated vasodilation in the RTN, which is the main brainstem region that regulates breathing, is regulated by purinergic signaling and that this mechanism is specialized to prevent vascular CO2/H+ reactivity and support the drive to breath.

purinergic regulation of RTN arterioles is the opposite of the rest of the brain, where purinergic regulation is vasodilatory, and that purinergic vasodilation is essential for the CO2/H+ ventilatory response.

1) P2Y2/P2Y4 receptors in the RTN are critical to the CO2 ventilatory response; 2) the CO2/H+-evoked vasodilator response is absent in the RTN; 3) the CO2-induced vasodilator effect is present in the rest of the brain and is P2Y2 and P2Y4 dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how CO2/H+ regulates the drive to breathe and how CO2/H+-sensitive neurons in the RTN regulate vascular tone in this region.
the role of the RTN in the regulation of breathing.
how the brain regulates its own blood supply to support its functions and behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
P2Y2 and/or P2Y4 receptors are responsible for the maintenance of vascular tone under hypercapnic conditions in the RTN and that this mechanism is essential for the CO2 ventilatory response.

P2Y2 and P2Y4 receptors in the RTN are involved in CO2/H+-sensitive regulation of vascular tone and that this regulation is specialized to support CO2/H+ chemosensitivity in this region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we discovered that the purinergic system in the retrotrazepezoid nucleus maintains vascular tone and that this mechanism is specialized to support CO2/H+ sensing.
purinergic regulation of RTN arteriolar tone is specialized to support CO2/H+-evoked increases in neuronal activity and breathing, while maintaining vascular tone.

we discovered a unique purinergic mechanism in the retrotrazepeoid nucleus (RTn) that maintains arteriole constriction during hypercapnia and disruption of this pathway decreases the CO2 ventilatory response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
purinergic regulation of the vascular tone in the brainstem is specialized to support breathing.
the RTN is a unique region within the brain that has adapted a mechanism for preventing vasodilation in response to CO2/H+ to ensure a robust drive to breathe.
chemosensitive areas in the brain have adapted mechanisms to maintain blood flow during high CO2.
